claims.claim: Normative documents and the single-NEXT roadmap retain TASK-424’s integrated interactive PRIMARY configuration, published v2 behavior, historical lineage and retired staging gates.

The native adapter supports one bounded Codex process, connection and thread across turns, preserves the selected profile, privately reauthenticates account updates and explicitly stops when identity is unsupported or changed.

Runtime checkpoint admission now accepts the existing bounded worker grammar while preserving authored commands, clean committed candidates and complete stable proof requirements for preterminal checkpoint sealing and factual feedback.

The installed native session consumed feedback and committed distinct C2 during focused local checking. Runtime enforces receipt, turn, source, lease, consent and checkpoint continuity before accepting correction.
Protected accounting retains two corrections, three checkpoints, 240-minute wall and 180-minute verification defaults, interrupted-reservation STOP and final checkpoint reuse for one terminal result.
Interactive PRIMARY remains separately authenticated through new-RUN version-3 consent; version-1, version-2, legacy and unsupported correction-operation routes retain their existing boundaries.

Focused tests cover native C1/F1/C2, first-pass completion, feedback forgery, lost authority/session/source, resource exhaustion and terminal contention. Repair adds toolchain and account-identity regressions and corrects STOP exception expectations.

Bounded original-RUN observations retain source/session/turn correlation, actual checkpoint and correction counts, verification consumption, unavailable evidence and final status, with review and publication explicitly unobserved.
